newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices mixed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices mixed in late trading.

text.p: U.S. cash crude oil prices were mixed in late trading on Tuesday amid bearish expectations for weekly American Petroleum Institute data, traders said.
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing softened slightly to around $19.60-70 a barrel, up five cents from late Monday's cash market.
July WTI/Cushing was pegged around five cents ahead of June, up from a four-cent negative spread earlier today.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was steady at $1.80-84 a barrel, with $1.82 trading earlier, traders said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James eased back into negative territory to talk at WTI/Cushing minus two cents to flat. Flat last traded after trading as high as plus four cents earlier.
The grade was driven higher by earlier news that a U.S. company had bowed out of ULCC Laconia loading around May 5-14 and destined to bring Brent to the Gulf Coast.
The news reinforced the view that fewer North Sea cargoes would be heading toward the Gulf as a result of a narrowing transatlantic arbitrage.
WTI/Midland was a penny firmer at WTI/Cushing minus 31-29 cents. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was talked narrower at minus 45-38 cents a barrel.
West Texas Sour/Midland changed hands at WTI/Cushing minus $1.60, $1.65 and $1.68 after earlier moving at minus $1.70.
Tradersa attributed the sour uptick to pent-up buying and the narrowing arbitrage.
Lightly traded Eugene Island was tighter at minus $1.50-45, with $1.45 switching hands.
